topics.topic: Handling noncompliant room names already present in imported projects
questions: How are existing room names in an imported project reviewed and corrected before they reach the agent, given that the import preserves rooms, the import-time renaming action names only project display names and aliases, and rooms can never be renamed or removed?
What happens when a selected VPS project already contains a room name that breaks the rule, given that the import preserves rooms and rooms can neither be renamed nor removed?
How are existing room names in imported projects checked or corrected before they can reach the agent, given that import preserves rooms and a room can never be renamed or removed?

quotes:
As in R0-68 and R0-90, this is a rule on the writer — the owner, and the agent
through Kernel — not a check of Registry: Registry cannot tell what a word
means, refuses no name for its content and searches no text for words; a
name that breaks the rule does reach the agent.

The owner learns the rule from the governance's rules for writers, read
before the import (R0-79), where the names of imported projects are set
(R0-85); the owner interface does not show it, and Registry promises nothing
of a name the owner writes against it, as for R0-68 and R0-90.
judgement.why: The texts expressly make the rule a writer obligation rather than an import check and say that a noncompliant name is not refused and does reach the agent.

topics.topic: Verifying first-release agent instructions and blocking writes when verification fails
questions: What observable check proves that the exact rule is installed and effective for every agent session before production, and what blocks or disables production agent writes when that check fails?

Who verifies that the required AGENTS.md change is installed and effective, what observable evidence proves it, and what prevents production or agent writes if installation fails or the installed file is stale?

What observable check establishes that the applicable agent actually loaded the required instruction, and what happens to release admission or agent writes if the file is missing, unreadable, stale or not in scope for the running agent?

quotes:
In the first
release the agent learns it from its instructions, which the platform
installs in the agent's home on the home server (Factory
`platform/home_server/workspace/AGENTS.md`); adding the rule there is the
platform's change, made before the first release goes into production.
judgement.why: Verification that an installed instruction is in scope and loaded, and the admission check that blocks a release on failure, belong to State 8 testing and admission rather than State 0 product behavior.

topics.topic: Whether standing approval permits prohibited room names without name-specific owner review
questions: When a room-add node has standing approval, is a fresh owner review of the exact name still required, or may the room be written without any opportunity for the owner to refuse a prohibited name?
When a flow has standing approval and proposes a noncompliant room name, is the write allowed without review or must it stop so the owner can refuse that exact name?

When a standing approval exists and the agent submits a prohibited room name, must the write proceed under the standing approval or be stopped for the owner's name-specific refusal, and by what actor can it be stopped when Registry does not inspect content?

quotes:
Each such write of the
agent waits for the owner's approval of its exact request, unless the owner
gave that flow version a standing approval for the node (K-08).

Whatever the agent was
told, each room it adds waits for the owner's approval of the exact request,
its name included (R0-99), unless the owner gave a standing approval; the
owner refuses a name that breaks the rule before it is written.
judgement.why: In a standing-approved add-room history, the first obligation permits execution without a fresh owner decision while the second requires the owner to refuse the prohibited exact name before Registry writes it.

witness.initial: An active project is granted to an agent session, and the owner has given the flow version standing approval for its add-room node.
events: The agent, through Cabinet Kernel, submits an add-room request whose name identifies a person's disability.
Kernel applies the standing approval and therefore does not stop for approval of that exact request.
Registry receives the request; it cannot inspect the name's meaning and otherwise accepts the write.
outcomes: The standing-approval exception lets the room be written without fresh owner review.
The owner must see and refuse the rule-breaking name before the room is written.
witness.observer: The owner and the agent reading the resulting room list.
basis:
A room name reaches the agent and so its AI provider (R0-68), and the agent
may write one itself (R0-41).

As in R0-68 and R0-90, this is a rule on the writer — the owner, and the agent
through Kernel — not a check of Registry: Registry cannot tell what a word
means, refuses no name for its content and searches no text for words; a
name that breaks the rule does reach the agent.

In Registry's derived manifest record (R0-78), adding a room, publishing a
pointer and withdrawing one are `state-transition`. Each such write of the
agent waits for the owner's approval of its exact request, unless the owner
gave that flow version a standing approval for the node (K-08).

topics.topic: Proving owner acknowledgment of the rule before import and enforcing the prerequisite
questions: What records or verifies that the owner read the applicable rule before import, and what happens if that prerequisite has not been completed?
What concrete action proves that the owner read the current rule before import, and what prevents or fails the import when that action has not occurred?

quotes:
The owner learns the rule from the governance's rules for writers, read
before the import (R0-79), where the names of imported projects are set
(R0-85); the owner interface does not show it, and Registry promises nothing
of a name the owner writes against it, as for R0-68 and R0-90.
judgement.why: The text deliberately places learning the rule in governance and outside the owner interface, so acknowledgment evidence and the procedure followed before import are State 7 operational notes rather than a Registry action or failure.

topics.topic: Authority and consistency between installed agent instructions and derived manifest rules
questions: From the second release onward, which copy is authoritative if the installed agent instruction and the derived manifest description differ, and must release admission verify that their rule text or semantics agree?

quotes:
In the first
release the agent learns it from its instructions, which the platform
installs in the agent's home on the home server (Factory
`platform/home_server/workspace/AGENTS.md`); adding the rule there is the
platform's change, made before the first release goes into production. In
the second release (R0-100) the description of the room name and the alias in
Registry's manifest record (R0-78) carries it as well.

The design of what the second release holds — models, rules, routes,
contracts — is decided by that change's own states and rounds, as any change
of this specification; this decision fixes what it must hold, not how.
judgement.why: State 0 requires both representations to carry the same rule and explicitly defers their design, while detecting a stale or inconsistent generated or installed representation at admission belongs to State 8.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
